summary.text: 见 means “see” or “observe.” It is the standardized simplified form of 見, whose ancient graphic analysis combines an eye with a human figure to depict seeing. The lower figure is interpreted differently for ancient and received forms.

formation.text: The traditional graph 見 is a pictographic compound: the eye 目 and a human figure together depict a person seeing. Ancient forms are analyzed with 卩, interpreted as a kneeling person; the received form is parsed as 目 and 儿. The simplified graph 见 is a standardized simplified form of 見, though the evidence here does not trace its shape to a particular cursive exemplar.

components.text: In 見, 目 is the prominent eye and contributes to the depicted act of seeing. Ancient forms are analyzed with this eye element; the received-form analysis also identifies 目.

In the ancient-form analysis of 見, 卩 is interpreted as a kneeling person beneath the eye, completing the person-and-eye depiction. The received-form analysis instead parses its lower figure as 儿; the evidence treats these as stage-specific analyses, not corruption.
In the received-form analysis of 見, 儿 is the human figure paired with 目 in the depiction of seeing. This is a different analysis from the ancient-form account that identifies the lower figure as 卩.

history.text: Oracle-bone and bronze forms of 見 are indexed, and paleographic accounts describe ancient forms as a prominent eye above a human figure. The received dictionary analysis parses 見 as 儿 plus 目; the dossier does not establish a dated sequence of intermediate graphic changes.

The simplified-character standard maps 見 to 见. A source describes 见 as derived from cursive script, but the research did not verify a cursive exemplar or a detailed transition sequence, so that specific graphic path remains uncertain.

uncertainties.text: No specific earliest dated inscription was verified. Reported oracle-bone and bronze uses include seeing, audience, and other grammatical or lexical uses, but the available evidence does not establish their chronology or a complete sequence of meaning changes.

An oracle-bone use of 見 is reported as read 獻, “offer sacrificial goods.” This may be a case of reusing the graph to write a similar-sounding word, rather than a meaning developing from “see”; the inscription examples and independent sound comparison were not retrieved, so the borrowing account remains qualified. It does not establish the pronunciation of the depicted person or object.
The dossier includes a proposed Proto-Sino-Tibetan comparison, but the inspected evidence does not support it; no language-family etymology is asserted here.

senses.text: Seeing is the core meaning assigned to the graph by the received dictionary account and reported for oracle-bone and bronze uses. No specimen-level earliest date was verified.
Audience is reported among oracle-bone and bronze uses. The evidence does not date this use or establish how it relates chronologically to “see.”
A passive auxiliary use is reported for bronze inscriptions. Its chronology and development from the seeing sense are not established here.

senses.gloss: offer sacrificial goods, written with 見 and read 獻
senses.text: One reported oracle-bone use reads the graph as 獻, “offer sacrificial goods.” The proposed explanation is graph borrowing for a similar-sounding word, not a demonstrated semantic extension; the sound comparison and inscription-level evidence were not retrieved.
The current simplified character is glossed with meanings including seeing, observing, and perceiving.

limitations.text: The record supplies glosses and reported historical uses, but not a specimen-level date sequence sufficient to connect the audience, passive, and offering uses to one another or to the seeing sense.

overview.text: 见 means “see.” It is the simplified form of 見, whose eye and human figure together depict seeing; accounts differ on how to identify the lower figure in ancient and received forms.

components.text: The eye is emphasized as part of the picture of seeing.
In the ancient-form account, this is a kneeling person beneath the eye.
The received-form account identifies the lower figure as a person; it differs from the ancient-form identification.

relationships.text: In the traditional graph 見, 目 is the eye in the person-and-eye depiction of seeing.
The ancient-form analysis of 見 identifies 卩 as the kneeling person beneath the eye; the received-form account uses a different lower-form analysis.
The received-form analysis of 見 parses 儿 as the human figure paired with 目; this is distinct from the ancient-form analysis identifying 卩.
The standard maps traditional 見 to simplified 见.
